1.why: All six screens use a static, clean card layout with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups anywhere.

2.why: Bold step headings and solid blue primary buttons stand out clearly, though the large dark activity-log panel also competes for visual attention.

3.why: Each screen presents a single task with one input and one obvious primary action, so the needed element is quick to locate despite the extra simulation log and footer text.

4.why: Password rules and instructions are displayed on-screen at the moment of need and delivered codes remain visible in the log, though the flow spans six steps with several password rules.

5.why: No password-manager option, autofill affordance, or 'remember me' checkbox is shown anywhere; the inputs are plain empty fields.

6.why: The recovery token is pre-filled and delivered codes persist in the log for recognition, but the user must recall her own sign-in address with no saved-account cues displayed.

7.why: Instructions and bullet points are short and written in plain language, though technical text like 'https://localhost:3000' and 'evaluation simulation' adds jargon.

8.why: No error messages appear in any of the six screens, so there is no observable error text describing a problem or how to fix it.

9.why: Password requirements are stated as rules without a concrete example and fields lack placeholder examples, though the log explicitly displays the exact token and security code to enter.

10.why: The password and code steps that exist are clearly labeled, but no face-login or alternative authentication choices are offered, so the listed choice set is only partly present.

11.why: No screen offers more than two actions at once (e.g., 'Send recovery instructions' / 'I have a recovery code'), keeping simultaneous choices minimal.

12.why: The final screen explicitly confirms 'Your acceptance has been securely recorded' and each step heading plus the log reflect progress, though intermediate actions lack explicit success confirmations.

13.why: Every step carries a short guidance note or tip box, but there is no dedicated help link or support channel for a user who gets stuck.

14.why: A 'Back' button on step 2 and editable fields allow correction, but no resend-code option or error-retry feedback is visible.

15.why: All six steps share the identical header, card container, typography, button styling, and log placement, giving a highly consistent and learnable design.
